purpose: Versioned, evidence-backed mapping from registered components and their declared consumers to repository test targets for R/O/G pull-request validation.
claim_ceiling: This map selects repository validation only. It does not establish real-world causal effects, grant execution or publication authority, or replace required shared security, permission, evidence, review, or release checks.

Existing current-state sync, surface compilation, state-change, and task-identity advancement tests exercise the affected declared consumers.
Existing epistemic relationship, ESI human-surface, soft-governance authority, and durability tests exercise the declared G boundary consumers without granting truth or permission authority.

The existing federation contract, ownership and adversarial tests are extended with the registered Codex/Hermes/OpenClaw adapter tests, executor conformance/health/inventory and admission tests, plus the profile-declared live bridge and observation test family. These remain repository boundary checks and do not assert provider quality or external completion.

The existing Foundation test suite consumes formal-object records and schemas, while the canonical Lean Foundation proof command validates the formal proof consumer boundary. One execution covers both registered consumers.
Existing Foundation claim-governance and nonfunction-closure consumers validate L3 argument and claim relationships.
A focused test validates the existing historical rights-remediation register against its schema and reconciles its declared summary from the register entries without rewriting historical records.
These existing tests cover the registered no-L7 and system-map/front-door projection constraints.
These test modules are the existing registered consumers of Ignition Operating Method and its run-mode, capability, lifecycle, output and stranger-agent boundaries.
These existing publication and synchronization consumer tests cover L6/iteration publication constraints.
These existing consumers validate Foundation path classification and the propagation/era-resolution contracts affected by the L5 classification source.
Existing human-result and knowledge-experience validators and tests cover the registered human_knowledge_surfaces outputs and their derived consumers.

A stdlib trigger-coverage test binds the dedicated Q33 workflow to the human-front-door files, validators, projection inputs, fixtures, and its own regression test.

The Agent Runtime R0/R1 and profile consumer suites exercise the registered Kernel, Profile, runtime execution/configuration boundary and non-knowledge pilot, including self-escalation rejection, pack authority limits and bounded local execution.
The Pack registry/routing and repository-maintenance suites exercise registered domain and maintenance pack manifests, bounded capability selection and repository-local maintenance behavior.
Knowledge corpus admission and Knowledge Experience consumers exercise the registered knowledge pack intake and human-facing derived outputs without promoting evidence or claims.

The complete existing durability test family exercises the registered lifecycle, snapshot/tail, recovery, migration, namespace, revocation, accounting, pack-lifecycle and conservative unknown-effect boundaries.
The append-only ledger contract, durability/replay consumers and live/steering event consumers exercise the registered event ledger and its hash-chain, CAS, replay and snapshot-tail boundaries.

The existing Steering test family covers intent provenance, goal lifecycle, completion contracts, obligations, priority/conflict handling, drift, namespace, memory/profile boundaries, and explainable why-next behavior.
The REOS vNext minimal-kernel test directly exercises the bounded research-pack navigation and keeps it outside generic Kernel, authority and Owner definitions.
